NDT Level III consulting in San Antonio: aviation MRO, depot, vehicle and power-plant programs, and the local options

San Antonio's NDT work is anchored at Port San Antonio, where large aircraft and engine maintenance operations run their own NDT shops, and spreads out to vehicle assembly, defense contractors and power generation. Many of the big operators employ their own Level IIIs. Demand for an outside NDT Level 3 consultant comes from the suppliers, repair stations and smaller shops around them that need a written practice, procedures and examinations without a full-time hire. Atlantis provides that as ASNT NDT Level III consulting from Houston, roughly three hours east, with site visits when examinations or audits need them.

What do San Antonio companies ask a Level III for?

  • FAA repair stations certificated under 14 CFR Part 145: a written practice and NDT procedures that the repair station manual can reference, with personnel records an FAA inspector or airline auditor can follow.
  • Component and engine-part suppliers: penetrant and magnetic particle process control, and ultrasonic procedures traceable to OEM manual requirements.
  • Defense depot subcontractors supporting Air Force work, where the government's own NDI requirements sit beside the contractor's program.
  • Vehicle and heavy-equipment suppliers serving the city's truck plants: weld inspection procedures for frames and structures written to the customer's drawing notes.
  • Power plant contractors working boiler and turbine outages.

Rules and customer requirements around San Antonio

Repair stations work under 14 CFR Part 145 and their own FAA-accepted manuals, and airline customers audit against both. Air Force NDI runs under the Air Force Nondestructive Inspection program, which the Air Force's own fact sheet ties to Air Force Instruction 21-105, so contractors working beside depot staff often meet two sets of rules. Texas boiler and pressure vessel repairs fall under the TDLR Boiler Program, and radiography anywhere in Texas is done by the owner's licensed radiography contractor using DSHS-certified radiographers. If you arrived searching for NRTL field evaluations: those are evaluations of equipment, mostly electrical, by an OSHA-recognized testing laboratory, a different discipline from NDT and not something a Level III performs.

How the San Antonio options compare

  • In-house Level IIIs at the large MROs. StandardAero has recruited an NDT III engineer in San Antonio to write and approve procedures, examine and certify personnel, and run internal and external audits; that model suits operations big enough to keep a Level III busy.
  • Testing companies with local branches. Industrial Inspection & Analysis (IIA) lists a San Antonio location among its Texas sites and advertises ASNT Level III certification and program and procedure development.
  • Research organizations. Southwest Research Institute has an NDE Technology Section; technique and system development is a different job from maintaining a supplier's written practice.
  • National firms such as Mistras, Acuren and ATS, which describe Level III appointment, procedure development and audit services.
  • Remote outsourced Level IIIs such as Atlantis, for shops whose need is signed documents and clean records rather than a specialist on the payroll.

How to vet an NDT Level III consultant in San Antonio

  • For aviation work, ask how they reconcile the OEM's NDT manual with the written practice, and ask to see an example.
  • Check that the ASNT certificate covers PT and MT if those are your shop's processes; many component shops live on those two methods.
  • Ask whether they have prepared a repair station for an FAA or airline audit, and what the auditors sampled.
  • Ask who owns the examination question bank when the contract ends.
  • If the consultant's company sells NDT services to your customers, ask how they keep from steering work.

How Atlantis supports San Antonio companies

Atlantis's founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, is certified ASNT NDT Level III for UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, and Atlantis can be named as outside agency Level III for any of the five. Procedures, written practices and examinations are prepared remotely; practical examinations and audits take place at your facility. Aviation suppliers can start with aviation NDT consulting or aerospace NDT consulting; any shop can use written practice development, SNT-TC-1A training program setup and Level III documentation. For technicians, theory is self-paced online with Level III Q&A, practice runs in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on practical is held at the employer's facility; see NDT training in San Antonio. Send your scope through the San Antonio consulting request; we reply within one business day.
